- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.30), model frequently underestimates upward momentum — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for short-term (1–3 day) predictions.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often lags — delay upward adjustment by 1–2 days and apply gradual ramp-up (e.g., +0.2% per day).
- If model forecast is below 65.00 and sentiment is negative, avoid sharp downward moves — cap forecast at 65.00–67.00 to prevent overcorrection.
- For long-term (10+ days) forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for 10+ day horizon to reflect diminishing momentum.
